welcome.title: Welcome to AI Cockpit
welcome.body:
AI Cockpit — a local, offline-first console that orchestrates multiple AI agents from a single interface.

Quick start

  1. Pick a supplier card at the top (Claude, Gemini, Ollama, Workers).
  2. Type your prompt at the bottom and press Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line) to send.
  3. Responses appear in the chat panel. Use the sidebar tabs for files, code, plans, and more.

Press F1 over any element for context help, or ? for this full guide.

By Dario Ruggi — all processing is local unless you explicitly use a paid API provider.

suppliers.title: Supplier cards
suppliers.body:
The top strip shows one card per AI backend. Click a card to make it the active agent — all prompts go to it.

Cards

  • Claude / Codex / Qwen Code — Card 1's provider (Supplier Slots) picks which paid-subscription CLI runs here: Claude Code, Codex, or Qwen Code. Supports effort levels (low → max) and tool use. Runs in a tmux session.
  • Gemini / Groq — Card 2's provider (Supplier Slots) picks Gemini CLI or Groq (free-tier REST, no local binary — dispatched via Workers' encrypted key store instead of tmux). Gemini supports effort levels; Groq doesn't need one.
  • Ollama / LocalAI / Dual — Local LLM(s) (Qwen, Llama, Gemma, etc.). Free, private, offline. Card 3's provider (Supplier Slots) picks Ollama, LocalAI, or both at once (Dual mode — load one of each, run Power Combos across both). Pick a model or combo from the dropdown; a single model runs in a tmux session, Dual mode's second slot and Power Combos dispatch over HTTP instead.
  • Workers — Free-tier online API providers (Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras, etc.). Each has its own API key and quota.
  • Tools — Local CLI programs (ffmpeg, whisper, pandoc) for file conversions.

Card elements

  • Model dropdown — pick which model to use.
  • Effort dropdown (Claude/Gemini) — controls reasoning depth.
  • Usage bar — shows tokens used. Right-click to reset session stats.
  • Tune button settings — edit model list, effort options, and card config (JSON).

Session controls (top-right)

  • Start — launch all agent tmux sessions.
  • Stop — stop all sessions. Counter shows running count.
  • Restart — stop + start all.

The status bar beneath the supplier strip shows each agent's status (running / not running) and token counts.

effort.title: Effort levels
effort.body:
Claude and Gemini support an effort parameter that controls how much reasoning the model applies.

LowQuick, minimal reasoning. Good for simple questions.
MediumBalanced. Default for most tasks.
HighMore thorough reasoning. Better for complex tasks.
Extra (xhigh)Extended thinking. Good for hard problems.
MaxMaximum reasoning. Slowest, highest token usage.

Higher effort = more tokens consumed = faster quota depletion. Pick the level that matches the task complexity.

Edit the available options via the tune settings button on the supplier card.

modes.title: Modes
modes.body:
The mode strip controls how your prompt is dispatched.

SingleSend to the currently active agent only. Standard mode.
PipelineChain multiple agents: A → B → C. Each agent's output becomes the next agent's input. Check 2+ agents in the agent checkboxes below.
BroadcastSend the same prompt to all checked agents simultaneously. Compare answers side by side.
PlanOrchestrator mode. A strong planner decomposes your goal into steps. You can then Run, Sequence, or Schedule the plan. See the Plans topic for details.

The agent checkboxes (Claude, Gemini, Ollama) below the mode strip control which agents participate in Pipeline and Broadcast modes.

styles.title: Styles
styles.body:
Styles prepend an instruction to every prompt, steering how the agent should respond.

ChatConversational — answers in prose, no code unless asked.
OutlinePlan first, then implement. Agent lays out the approach before writing code.
ResearchExplore and explain. Detailed analysis with sources and reasoning.
BuildDefault builder mode. Agent writes working code directly.
DebugFocus on finding and fixing bugs. Step-by-step diagnosis.
AnalyzeDeep analysis of code, data, or architecture.
ReportStructured output — formal report format with sections and conclusions.

In Plan mode, the style prefix is NOT prepended to the orchestrator goal — it only applies to direct agent prompts.

prompt.title: Prompt area
prompt.body:
The prompt input

Type your message in the text area at the bottom. Resize it by dragging the top edge.

  • Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line) — send the prompt.
  • ↑ / ↓ arrow — cycle through prompt history (shell-style; the scope is this chat, this project or everywhere).
  • History button or Ctrl+R — filter every earlier prompt, then choose one: it goes into the box, it is not sent.
  • Esc — cancel an in-flight request.
  • Right-click — Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Save to Snippets/Library.

Buttons

  • EXECUTE — send (same as Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line)).
  • CLEAR — clear the prompt box.
  • SAVE — save the prompt text to Snippets or Library.

Toolbar buttons

  • Translate chat — translate all messages (via local LibreTranslate). Code blocks excluded.
  • Translate text — open a free-text translation box.
  • Summarize — summarize the current chat session.
  • Skills — open the Skills manager (reusable prompt templates).
  • Track — start/stop time tracking. Right-click for time report.
  • Image / Sound / Video — generate media locally (see Generation topic).

Caveman mode

The Caveman toggle (bottom right) controls response terseness. Off = normal prose. On = terse, fragment-style responses. Separate from agent sessions.

chat.title: Chat console
chat.body:
The central panel displays messages from you and the agents. Each message shows:

  • Line number (left margin) — for reference.
  • Agent tag — colored label (CLAUDE, GEMINI, OLLAMA, DARIO, System).
  • Timestamp and duration (how long the agent took).
  • Model label — which model generated the response.
  • Copy / Save buttons — on each agent response.

Right-click context menu

Select text in the chat and right-click to get: Copy, Select All, Save to Snippets, Save to Library.

Search

Ctrl+F opens a search bar at the top. Matches are highlighted; use arrow buttons to jump between them.

Code blocks & folding

Code in responses is syntax-highlighted with Copy and Save to Snippets buttons. Long code blocks (over 15 lines) are auto-collapsed — click the header bar to expand/collapse. The header shows language, line count, and action buttons.

System message folding

When 4 or more consecutive system messages appear, they are automatically grouped into a collapsible section to reduce clutter. Click to expand/collapse the group.

Markdown rendering

Responses are rendered with markdown: bold, italic, headings, lists, code blocks, tables, links.

rules.title: Rules / Directives
rules.body:
Global standing rules that are prepended to every agent prompt. Write rules once — they apply to Claude, Gemini, Ollama, and text Workers automatically.

How they work

  • Rules are inserted before your prompt text at dispatch time.
  • A compact variant is used for tiny models (≤4B) that can't handle long preambles.
  • Per-project rules live in each project's COCKPIT.md file and layer on top of global rules.

Editing

Click the Rules button (top bar) to open the directives editor. Changes apply immediately to subsequent prompts.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.body:
Capabilities are MCP servers (Claude/Gemini) and tool-shims (Ollama) that extend what agents can do.

Types

  • Built-in — shipped with Cockpit (e.g., step-cap, failure-halt, loop-detector, sequence-logger). Cannot be deleted.
  • User-defined — your own CAP.json files. Can be edited and deleted.

Toggle

Each capability has an ON/OFF switch at the left of its row — a bordered box that reads OFF or ON. The staged configuration is refreshed with every prompt, so a change reaches the agent from your next prompt. When ON, it's injected as a system prompt or tool definition into the agents that support it.

Guardrail capabilities

Four built-in capabilities support the Plan-and-Sequence system:

  • step-cap — limits maximum steps per sequence run.
  • failure-halt — halts after N consecutive failures.
  • loop-detector — detects near-identical retry loops via text similarity.
  • sequence-logger — writes structured JSONL run logs.

plans.title: Plans & Orchestrator
plans.body:
Plan mode decomposes a goal into structured steps using multiple agents as voters.

Creating a plan

  1. Switch to Plan mode.
  2. Type your goal (e.g., "Add unit tests for auth module").
  3. Press Execute. The orchestrator asks each checked agent to propose a plan, then synthesizes the best one.

Plan toolbar buttons

RunExecute now with assigned agents (Claude/Gemini/Ollama). Interactive, uses paid CLI tokens. Each step runs sequentially with approval gates.
SequenceExecute with local Ollama model only. Each step gets isolated context + verification gate + loop detection. Free, private, slower. Best for mechanical tasks.
ScheduleSchedule a Sequence run for later (e.g., overnight). Runs unattended via cron with all guardrails active. Review the JSONL log in the morning.
VotesShow the original plans each voter agent proposed before synthesis.
PausePause a running/sequencing plan (visible only while executing).
Re-RunReset all steps to pending and re-run. Previous results are lost. Shown on completed/halted/failed plans.
DeletePermanently remove the plan.

Plan-and-Sequence pattern

A strong planner (Claude/Gemini) decomposes once. A weak local model (Ollama, ≤4B) executes atomic steps with verification gates. Each step must be atomic, stateless, and verifiable. Guardrails (step-cap, failure-halt, loop-detector) prevent runaway execution.

Remote A2A agents in plans

Plan steps can be assigned to remote A2A agents using a2a:agent_id as the agent name. The synthesizer automatically sees registered A2A agents and may assign them to steps. A2A steps run synchronously — Cockpit sends the prompt, polls until done, and stores the result.

  • Retry — A2A steps retry up to 2 times with backoff on failure.
  • Timeout — 5 minutes per A2A step (configurable).

voice.title: Voice input
voice.body:
The microphone button records your voice and transcribes it locally using whisper.cpp — audio never leaves your machine. Press to start, press again to stop. The words appear in the prompt box for editing before you send, with a line saying how long you recorded and which model ran.

You can see it working: while you record, a bar with a pulsing red dot opens to the left of the button and moves with your voice, and the button itself fills as the level rises. If it does not move, the microphone is muted or the wrong input is selected.

The ▾ menu

  • Model — whisper model size. Bigger = more accurate, slower. Auto = the one pinned in whisper_config.json, else the largest installed; the label shows which.
  • Language — the language you speak: every language whisper supports, English by default, remembered. Forcing a language avoids a short clip being taken for a similar-sounding language.
  • Mic — which input to record from. The default is often an empty analog jack; the real microphone may be on a USB camera or headset.
  • Test level — listens for 4 seconds and says Good, Silent or Clipping.

A microphone you picked earlier that is no longer plugged in is forgotten, and the default input is used.

The Language list holds every language whisper understands (English by default; Auto-detect is available but can mishear Hebrew). Your pick is remembered.

workers.title: Workers (paid & free)
workers.body:
Workers are online LLM API providers used as specialty engines or direct answering agents.

Free-tier workers

Providers like Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras, SambaNova, and Z.ai (GLM) offer free quotas. Each has rate limits (calls/day, tokens/day) tracked in the Usage tab. Z.ai exposes the GLM family (GLM-4.6/4.5/4.5-Air, plus free -flash models) — get a key at z.ai.

Paid API workers (BYOK)

Bring Your Own Key providers (OpenAI, Claude API, Gemini API) that cost real money per call.

  • Consent gate — paid spend must be explicitly enabled in Settings with a consent checkbox.
  • Global monthly cap — set a dollar limit. The system blocks calls that would exceed it.
  • Per-model caps — set individual caps per model.
  • 80% warning — a system message alerts you when spend reaches 80% of any cap.
  • Overshoot — caps are best-effort. Spend can overshoot by one call (the call in flight when the cap is crossed).

Discover

Click Discover to fetch each provider's model list from their API. Click + to add a model to the selectable list.

API keys

Paste keys in the Workers settings. Keys are stored locally in cockpit_data/workers_keys.json.

tools.title: Tools
tools.body:
Local CLI programs for file conversions and transforms. No internet, no API keys required.

Available tools

Tools include ffmpeg (video/audio), whisper (transcription), pandoc (document conversion), ImageMagick, and more. Enable/disable per tool.

Presets

Each tool has presets — pre-configured command templates. Pick a preset, select input files, and run. Output appears in the chat.

Auto-routing

Agents can auto-route to tools via %%TOOL:toolname%% markers in their output.

jobs.title: Jobs (Scheduler)
jobs.body:
The scheduler runs tasks on a timer (cron-driven) or on demand.

Job types

  • plan_sequence — run a Plan-and-Sequence overnight. Ticks through steps, polls for output, verifies each step.
  • Custom jobs — any command in the allowed whitelist.

Status

  • Pending — waiting for its scheduled time.
  • Running — currently executing. Jobs stuck running >15 min are auto-marked failed.
  • Done — completed successfully.
  • Failed — finished with errors.

Controls

  • Run now — execute a job immediately.
  • Cancel — stop a pending/running job.
  • Delete — remove from history.

The Jobs button in the Toolbar shows how many jobs exist in a small chip; the chip takes the accent colour while any are pending or running (hover for the numbers).

accumulator.title: Accumulator
accumulator.body:
The Accumulator extracts reusable knowledge from PDFs and documents using a local pipeline.

Pipeline

  1. Extract — PDF → text (pdftotext, tika, or Ollama OCR fallback).
  2. Chunk — split into overlapping segments.
  3. Summarize — Ollama generates a summary per chunk.
  4. Store — results saved as JSON for retrieval.

Panel tabs

  • Queue — files waiting to be processed.
  • Results — processed documents with summaries.
  • Health — pipeline health check (extractors + Ollama reachability).

Click Run to process the queue. Progress is shown live.

themes.title: Themes & Theming
themes.body:
Built-in themes

Several themes ship with Cockpit (dark, light, mixed modes). Switch via the theme toggle button (top bar).

Theme editor

Click the Theme Editor button to open a full color editor with grouped pickers: backgrounds, text, borders, agent colors, and accents. Changes preview in real time in a sandbox strip.

  • Apply — apply colors to the live UI (session only).
  • Save As — persist as a new named theme.
  • Delete — remove a user theme (built-in themes are read-only).

Importing themes

  • VS Code themes — import a .json VS Code color theme. Colors are mapped to Cockpit variables automatically.
  • Export/Import — export all themes as JSON, import on another machine.

All UI elements follow the theme

Modals, context menus, confirm dialogs, sidebar tabs, code blocks, data bars — everything uses CSS variables from the active theme.

Protanopia-safe design

Cockpit never uses color alone to convey meaning. No red/green-only indicators. Blue, cyan, amber, orange, and violet are the primary accent palette.

left-sidebar.title: Left sidebar
left-sidebar.body:
The left sidebar has three tabs:

Chats

List of chats in the current project. Each chat is an independent conversation thread.

  • + New — create a new chat.
  • Double-click a chat name to rename it.
  • Import/Export buttons — save/load chat JSON files.
  • Detach — move a chat to the Free (standalone) pool.
  • Delete — remove a chat permanently.

Projects

Group chats by project. Each project gets its own COCKPIT.md for project-specific rules, a file tree, and isolated context.

  • + New — create a project.
  • Config (COCKPIT.md) — edit the project's per-project rules.
  • Delete — remove the project and all its chats.

Files

Browse the project's working directory as a file tree. Click a file to preview it in the right sidebar.

right-sidebar.title: Right sidebar
right-sidebar.body:
The right sidebar has multiple tabs:

PreviewLive preview of HTML/Markdown files. Updates when you select a file from the file tree.
CodeCode editor with syntax highlighting, find/replace, line numbers. Edit project files inline.
LibrarySaved references — URLs, file paths, notes. Scopeable to project or global.
SnippetsReusable code fragments with language tags. Save from chat (F2) or add manually.
SourcesSource code files used as context or reference material.
ConfigConfiguration panel — storage paths, attachment routes, import/export settings.
SearchWeb search integration — search, read results, inject into prompt context.
CapabilitiesMCP servers and tool-shims. Toggle ON/OFF per capability.
PlansOrchestrator plans — view steps, run/sequence/schedule, inspect votes.
AttachmentsFiles attached to the current chat. Upload, manage, and reference in prompts.
UsageToken usage and quota tracking for all suppliers and workers.

Pending Proposals

Below the tabs, the Pending Proposals section shows agent suggestions (file edits, commands) awaiting your approval. Approve or reject individually or in batch.

usage.title: Usage & Data bars
usage.body:
Supplier card data bars

Each supplier card shows a compact usage meter — a thin colored bar showing tokens consumed relative to the quota or context window.

  • Claude — tokens used vs. the ~44K 5-hour rolling window. Bar fills amber as you approach the limit.
  • Gemini — tokens used with cache savings percentage.
  • Ollama — prompt/output tokens. No external quota (local model). Bar shows context window fill.
  • Workers — calls used vs. daily/hourly free-tier quota per provider.

Usage tab (right sidebar)

Detailed breakdown by range (Today / Week / Month / All time):

  • Claude section — input/output tokens, cache read/write, total, sessions, messages, 5h window reset countdown.
  • Gemini section — input/output, cached, thoughts, cost note.
  • Ollama section — prompt/output tokens, calls, avg latency, by-model breakdown.
  • Paid API spend — total USD spent this month, per-model breakdown, cap usage bars. Amber bar turns orange at 80%.
  • Workers (free tiers) — per-provider call counts with quota bars. Colors: cyan (OK), amber (>60%), orange (>85%).

Right-click reset

Right-click the Ollama or Workers usage area in the supplier strip to reset session counters.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body:
Skills are reusable prompt templates with auto-trigger capability.

Creating skills

Open Skills manager → + New. Each skill has:

  • Name — identifier (used as /trigger command).
  • Description — what it does and when to use it. The description coach scores your description and suggests improvements.
  • Tier — priority level for auto-matching.
  • Content — the prompt template (supports variables).

Auto-trigger

When enabled, skills auto-fire based on keyword overlap + trigram similarity scoring against your prompt. The system scores each skill and injects the best match above a threshold.

Folder skills

Skills can also be defined as SKILL.md files in cockpit_data/skills/<name>/ directories, with YAML frontmatter for metadata.

Built-in skill: Plan-and-Sequence

The plan-and-sequence skill teaches the planner to emit atomic, verifiable steps suitable for weak local model execution.

models.title: Model Manager (F8)
models.body:
Press F8 to open the Ollama Model Manager.

Features

  • Pull — download a model from the Ollama registry. Progress is shown live.
  • Browse — search a curated catalog of popular models.
  • Remove — delete a model (frees disk space).
  • Details — view model info (parameters, Modelfile, etc.).
  • Probe — test if a model supports tool calls (4-check pipeline: health → model present → Messages API → tool-call round-trip). Shows AGENTIC CAPABLE or NOT AGENTIC.
  • Variant — create an agentic-tuned variant with custom Modelfile (num_ctx, temperature, repeat_penalty). Variants are tagged with an AGENTIC badge.

Runtime knobs

At the bottom of the Model Manager:

  • keep_alive — how long models stay loaded after last use (default: 5m).
  • num_ctx — context window size in tokens (default: 4096). Higher = more memory.
  • num_parallel — concurrent requests per model (default: 1).
  • max_loaded — max models loaded simultaneously (default: 1).

Click Save knobs to persist. Changes take effect on the next agent session restart.

generate.title: Media generation
generate.body:
Generate media locally using your GPU — no internet, no cost.

Image

Powered by stable-diffusion.cpp (SD 1.5). Pick a preset (Logo, Icon, FavIcon, Background, Image), type a prompt, click Generate. ~20 seconds per image. Results appear inline with Save/Download/Delete buttons.

Sound

Powered by Piper TTS. Type text, generate spoken audio (WAV). Player appears inline.

Video

Renders several frames with varying seeds via sd.cpp, then assembles an animated GIF with ffmpeg. Slower (~2–3 min).

All generated files go to cockpit_data/generated/ and are served inline in the chat.

search.title: Web search
search.body:
The Search tab in the right sidebar provides web search integration.

  • Type a query and search.
  • Results show title, URL, and snippet.
  • Open — open the URL in a new browser tab.
  • Read & Insert — fetch the page content and inject it into your prompt as context.
  • Save to Library — save the URL as a Library reference.

Note: search engines increasingly refuse automated queries, so a search can come back empty even when your network is fine. Cockpit says which engine refused.

editor.title: Code editor
editor.body:
A floating, draggable, resizable code editor for editing project files, snippets, skills, and config.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting — Prism.js: Pascal, PHP, Bash, JavaScript, JSON, CSS, HTML, Python, SQL, YAML, and more.
  • Find & replace — Ctrl+F opens find/replace bar.
  • Line numbers — toggle on/off.
  • Word wrap — toggle on/off.
  • Language picker — switch highlighting language.
  • Tab inserts 2 spaces (not a tab character).
  • Save / Save as… — persist changes back to disk.

translate.title: Translation
translate.body:
Translation uses local LibreTranslate — no data leaves your machine.

Translate chat

Translates all messages in the current chat. Code blocks are excluded (preserved as-is). Pick source and target languages.

Translate text

Opens a free-text translation box. Paste any text, pick languages, translate. Result can be copied or inserted into the prompt.

time.title: Time tracking
time.body:
The Track button starts/stops a timer for the current project.

  • Click to start tracking. Click again to stop.
  • The button shows elapsed time while tracking.
  • Right-click → Time report: view logged time entries.
  • Entries can be deleted individually.

The counter in the top-right ("59" etc.) shows total tracked minutes for the current session.

context-menus.title: Context menus
context-menus.body:
Cockpit replaces all browser context menus with themed, app-native menus.

Chat panel (right-click on selected text)

  • Copy
  • Select All
  • Save to Snippets
  • Save to Library

Prompt area (right-click)

  • Cut (when text selected)
  • Copy (when text selected)
  • Paste
  • Select All
  • Save to Snippets / Library (when text selected)

Special right-clicks

  • Ollama usage bar → Reset Ollama session stats
  • Workers usage bar → Reset Workers usage
  • Time button → Open time report

Input fields (text inputs, textareas, dropdowns) retain the native browser menu for paste/spell-check.

proposals.title: Pending Proposals
proposals.body:
When agents suggest file edits or actions, they appear in the Proposals tab of the right sidebar (a count shows on its icon from any tab).

  • Approve — accept and apply the proposal.
  • Reject — discard it.
  • Approve All / Reject All — batch actions.

Proposals are per-chat and persist until acted upon.

sessions.title: Session controls
sessions.body:
The sessions card (top right) holds the process controls and, in the native window, the window controls:

ExitShows what is running and the ways to stop it: close the window only, stop the agent sessions, or stop everything (web server included). In the native window the ▁ ▢ glyphs beside it minimise / maximise when the frame is off.
Start / StopLaunch or terminate the agent tmux sessions (Card 1, Card 2, local). The chip on the button shows how many are running (e.g. "3/3"); Start replaces Stop when none are.
RestartStop + Start all sessions and reload the page. Useful after changing Ollama knobs or rules.
ReopenCloses and reopens the native window (applies a frame change under Wayland; picks up a new shell binary after an upgrade).
ReloadHard-reloads the app, bypassing the cache (what a deploy does automatically).
RefreshRe-reads status, account and machine state now instead of waiting for the next poll.
⛶Frameless: the window drops its title bar (live on X11, on Reopen under Wayland/WSLg). Double-click the header to maximise, drag it to move.

On first load, a modal asks whether to start sessions automatically. In a plain browser only Exit / Start / Stop / Restart show.

summarize.title: Summarize
summarize.body:
The Summarize button generates a summary of the current chat session using the active agent.

  • Summarizes all messages (user + agent) in the current chat.
  • The summary appears as a new message in the chat.
  • Optionally save the summary to Library or Snippets.

Useful for creating a recap before switching to a new task or sharing context.

caveman.title: Caveman mode
caveman.body:
The Caveman toggle (bottom-right of prompt area) controls token compression for online suppliers (Claude, Gemini, Workers). Ollama (local) is never affected.

Levels

OffNormal prompts and responses. No compression.
StripRemoves filler words, articles, pleasantries from your prompt before sending. Saves ~30% tokens.
Strip+AIStrip mode + asks the agent to respond in terse caveman style. Saves ~60-75% tokens on both input and output.

Model selector

The dropdown next to the Caveman button selects which Ollama model to use for local tasks (default model for the Ollama agent card).

typography.title: Font & typography
typography.body:
Font size controls (Settings card, top bar)

  • − / + buttons — decrease/increase font size by 1px.
  • Tt Aa button — open the full Typography panel for font family, line height, and spacing.
  • The current font size (e.g., "14.5px") is shown between the buttons.

Text style toggles (right sidebar footer)

  • B — toggle bold text in the console.
  • I — toggle italic text in the console.
  • U — toggle underline on message tags.

All typography settings are persisted in localStorage.

map.title: Unit Map
map.body:
The Map button (left sidebar, Files tab) scans the current project for Pascal and PHP source files and generates a structured unit map.

  • Lists all units/classes/functions found in each file.
  • Opens the map in the floating code editor (read-only).
  • Use it to get a quick overview of a project's code structure.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.body:
The Attachments tab (right sidebar) manages files attached to the current chat.

Features

  • Upload — drag & drop or click to attach files to the chat.
  • Inline — text/code files are shown inline in prompts for agent context.
  • Vision — images are described by a local vision model and injected as text.
  • Video — videos are processed in 3 steps: keyframe extraction (FFmpeg, up to 8 scene-change frames), vision description of each frame, and audio transcription (Whisper). The combined visual + audio summary is injected into the prompt.
  • Audio — audio files are transcribed via Whisper and inlined.
  • Documents — PDF, DOCX, etc. are converted to markdown via Pandoc.
  • Save only — files stored but not automatically included in prompts.

Video requirements

ffmpeg (keyframes + audio), Ollama with gemma3:4b (vision), whisper (transcription). Each is optional — missing tools are skipped gracefully.

Route overrides

In the Config tab, you can set per-extension routing rules (e.g., .pdf → inline-text, .png → image-vision, .mp4 → video-vision) to control how each file type is handled.

Attachments are stored per-chat in the project's storage directory.

terminal.title: Terminal button (top toolbar)
terminal.body:
The Terminal button opens the command window: type a simple command, see what it printed.

What it is

  • One command line at a time, run as you, in a folder you choose with cd (it starts in your Public folder).
  • Up / Down brings back earlier commands. help explains the limits; clear empties the window.

What confines it

  • The operating system (Landlock), not a list of allowed words: a command can write only in your Public folder, read your project folders and the usual programs, and nothing else on the machine is visible to it.
  • 20 seconds and 256 KB per command. If the machine cannot confine commands, none are run.
  • It is not a full terminal: no full-screen programs (nano, vim, top), no passwords. Network access is not restricted.

The small monitor button in the title bar opens the system terminal when this machine has one.

files-btn.title: Files button (top toolbar)
files-btn.body:
The Files button opens the file window, a floating window that works like a desktop file manager.

Your Public folder

  • Your own folder (inside your projects folder). Everything works there: new folder or file, rename, move (drag and drop), copy, upload (drag files in from your computer), download, delete.
  • Delete moves to the Trash; delete inside the Trash is permanent.

Everything else is read-only

  • Your project folders (and any area an admin added) can be looked at, viewed, downloaded and copied into Public. Nothing there can be changed.
  • Symbolic links are never followed, so a link cannot lead anywhere else.

Keys

Arrows, Enter, Backspace (up), F2 rename, Delete, Ctrl+C / X / V, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Shift+N new folder, F5 refresh, Ctrl+L type a path.

The small monitor button in the window's title bar opens the system file manager when this machine has one. The window needs the engine service (it is hosted by the process supervisor).

browser-btn.title: Browser button
browser-btn.body:
The Browser button opens an embedded web browser panel inside Cockpit.

  • Browse web pages without leaving the app.
  • Useful for checking documentation, testing local dev servers, or viewing generated HTML.
  • Content can be extracted and injected into prompts as context.

keys-btn.title: Keys button
keys-btn.body:
The Keys button opens the API key management panel.

  • Add, edit, and remove API keys for all suppliers (Claude, Gemini, Workers).
  • Keys are stored locally in cockpit_data/ — never sent anywhere except to the respective API.
  • Each provider shows its key status (set / not set).
  • Test buttons verify key validity by making a minimal API call.

execute-btn.title: Execute button
execute-btn.body:
The EXECUTE button sends the current prompt to the active agent. Same as pressing Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line).

  • In Single mode — sends to the selected supplier.
  • In Pipeline mode — starts the chain through checked agents.
  • In Broadcast mode — sends to all checked agents simultaneously.
  • In Plan mode — sends the goal to the orchestrator for decomposition.

The button is disabled while a request is in flight. Press Esc to cancel.

clear-btn.title: Clear button
clear-btn.body:
The CLEAR button empties the prompt text area. Does not affect chat history or any other state.

Keyboard shortcut: none (intentional — prevents accidental clearing).

save-btn.title: Save button (prompt)
save-btn.body:
The SAVE button saves the current prompt text to Snippets or Library.

  • A scope dialog asks whether to save to Project or Global scope.
  • Saved as a Snippet with language auto-detected from content.
  • Useful for preserving complex prompts you want to reuse later.

attach-btn.title: Attach button
attach-btn.body:
The Attach button opens a file picker to attach files to the current chat.

  • Attached files appear in the Attachments tab (right sidebar).
  • Text/code files are inlined into prompts automatically.
  • Images are described by a local vision model and injected as text.
  • Videos are analyzed: keyframes extracted and described, audio transcribed — combined summary injected into prompt.
  • Audio files are transcribed via Whisper.
  • You can also drag & drop or paste files directly.

left-files.title: Left sidebar — Files tab
left-files.body:
The Files tab in the left sidebar shows the project's working directory as a tree.

  • Click a file to open it in the right sidebar (Preview or Code editor).
  • Folders expand/collapse on click.
  • The Map button scans Pascal/PHP source files and generates a unit map.
  • The Refresh button reloads the tree from disk.
  • File icons indicate type (code, text, image, config).

left-projects.title: Left sidebar — Projects tab
left-projects.body:
The Projects tab lists all Cockpit projects. Each project groups chats, files, and context together.

  • + New — create a new project (name + working directory).
  • Click a project to switch to it — the chat list, file tree, and rules update.
  • Config — edit the project's COCKPIT.md (per-project rules and context).
  • Delete — remove the project and all its chats (with confirmation).
  • The Free pool holds chats not assigned to any project.

left-chats.title: Left sidebar — Chats tab
left-chats.body:
The Chats tab lists all conversation threads in the current project.

  • + New — start a fresh chat.
  • Click a chat to switch to it.
  • Double-click the name to rename.
  • Export — save chat as JSON.
  • Import — load a previously exported chat.
  • Detach — move chat to the Free (unassigned) pool.
  • Delete — permanently remove (with confirmation).

Each chat has independent history, attachments, and proposals.

right-tabs.title: Right sidebar — Tab buttons
right-tabs.body:
The right sidebar tab strip lets you switch between panels. Each tab button shows an icon and label:

PreviewLive HTML/Markdown preview of the selected file.
CodeInline code editor with syntax highlighting.
LibraryYour knowledge base — books, articles, magazines (PDF/EPUB/DOCX/MD…). Add a file via the picker or add a folder to scan; Cockpit extracts the text so it's keyword- and semantically searchable (the neurology Deep Search button). A place for you and agents to find solutions, techniques, and ideas.
SnippetsReusable code fragments.
SourcesSource files loaded as context.
ConfigSettings, routes, import/export.
SearchWeb search with inject-to-prompt.
CapsCapabilities (MCP servers, tool-shims).
PlansOrchestrator plans and step management.
AttachFile attachments for the current chat.
UsageToken usage and quota tracking.

Click a tab to switch. The active tab is highlighted with the accent color. Tab state persists across page loads.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body:
Cockpit settings are spread across several panels. Here is a complete reference.

Config tab (right sidebar → Config)

  • Storage path — root directory for all Cockpit data (chats, projects, snippets, library, attachments).
  • Attachment routes — per-extension rules controlling how attached files are handled (inline-text, image-vision, save-only). Add custom routes for any extension.
  • Import / Export — export all Cockpit data as a single JSON archive, or import from a previous export.

Supplier card tune (settings button on each card)

  • Model list — edit which models appear in the dropdown for each supplier.
  • Effort options (Claude/Gemini) — configure available effort levels.
  • Raw JSON config — advanced per-supplier overrides (API endpoints, parameters, etc.).

Ollama runtime knobs (Model Manager → bottom panel)

  • keep_alive — how long models stay loaded after last use (default 5m).
  • num_ctx — context window size in tokens (default 4096).
  • num_parallel — concurrent requests per model (default 1).
  • max_loaded — maximum models loaded simultaneously (default 1).
  • Saved to ollama_config.json; takes effect on next session restart.

Workers API keys

  • Set via the Workers card → Keys panel.
  • Stored locally in cockpit_data/workers_keys.json.
  • Each provider (Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras, etc.) has its own key field.

Paid API spend controls

  • Consent gate — paid API calls require explicit opt-in.
  • Global monthly cap — maximum USD spend per month across all paid providers.
  • Per-model caps — individual spend limits per model.
  • 80% warning system message triggers automatically.

Theme settings

  • Switch themes via the toggle button (top bar).
  • Full theme editor with live preview — backgrounds, text, borders, accents.
  • Import VS Code themes, export/import custom themes.

Typography

  • Font size +/− buttons (bottom toolbar).
  • Tt Aa button opens full typography panel (font family, line height, spacing).
  • B / I / U toggles for console text style.

Rules / Directives

  • Global rules prepended to every prompt.
  • Per-project rules in COCKPIT.md.
  • Compact variant auto-selected for small models (≤4B).

Capabilities

  • Toggle MCP servers and tool-shims ON/OFF per capability.
  • Built-in guardrails: step-cap, failure-halt, loop-detector, sequence-logger.

Voice input

  • Language override (a two-letter code such as FR or DE).
  • Whisper model size selection.

Persistence

Most settings persist in localStorage or in cockpit_data/ JSON files. Theme, font size, sidebar state, and panel sizes are restored on reload.

walkthrough.title: Walkthrough — Getting Started
walkthrough.body:
1. Launch agents

Click Start (top-right) to launch Claude, Gemini, and Ollama tmux sessions. The status dots turn green when running.

2. Pick a supplier

Click a supplier card (Claude, Gemini, Ollama, Workers, Tools) to make it active. All prompts go to the active supplier.

3. Choose mode & style

Mode controls dispatch: Single (one agent), Pipeline (chain), Broadcast (all at once), Plan (orchestrator). Style steers response format: Chat, Build, Debug, Research, etc.

4. Or let it fly — Autopilot Cruise

Instead of picking a mode, type a goal in the prompt box and press flight PLAN in the Hive section of the left sidebar. Cockpit plans it into steps, runs them as a durable, resumable chain, and posts the answer back. Enter always dispatches normally — planning happens only when you press PLAN. (The Hive section also shows which agents are up and which chains are running; its Agents, Chains and Broker buttons open the panel scoped to that view — that's AutoCognition.)

5. Write and send

Type in the prompt area at the bottom. Press Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line) or click EXECUTE. Responses appear in the chat panel.

5. Attach files

Drag files onto the chat or click Attach. Text files are inlined as context; images go to vision models.

6. Use the right sidebar

Tabs give you: Preview (HTML/MD live view), Code (editor), Library (saved refs), Snippets (code fragments), Sources (context files), Search (web), Capabilities (MCP tools), Plans (orchestrator), Attachments, Usage (quotas).

7. Manage projects

Left sidebar → Projects tab. Create projects to group chats, files, and per-project rules (COCKPIT.md).

8. Plan & orchestrate

Switch to Plan mode. Type a goal. The orchestrator decomposes it into steps. Then: Run (interactive, paid CLI), Sequence (local Ollama, free), or Schedule (cron, overnight).

9. Local tools

Click Tools card for file conversions (ffmpeg, whisper, pandoc, ImageMagick). Pick a preset, select files, run.

10. Generate media

Image (stable-diffusion.cpp), Sound (Piper TTS), Video (animated GIF) — all local, free, GPU-powered.

11. Voice input

Click the mic button to dictate. Transcription is local (whisper.cpp). Edit the transcript before sending.

12. Translation

Translate chat translates all messages (code excluded). Translate text opens a free-text box. Both use local LibreTranslate.

13. Time tracking

Click Track to start/stop a timer. Right-click for the time report.

14. Skills

Reusable prompt templates with auto-trigger. Open Skills manager to create, edit, and organize.

15. Keyboard shortcuts

Enter (Ctrl/Shift+Enter for a new line)Send
EscCancel / close modal
F1Context help
F2 / F3Save to Snippets / Library
F8Model Manager
↑ / ↓Prompt history
Ctrl+FSearch chat / editor

16. Themes

Toggle dark/light, or open the Theme Editor for full customization. Import VS Code themes. All UI follows the active theme.

17. Caveman mode

Toggle bottom-right to compress prompts/responses and save tokens on paid suppliers.

Not the same thing as a caveman plugin installed in your own terminal CLI. That one is a SessionStart hook in ~/.claude and runs before Cockpit's prompt, so Cockpit cannot switch it off — answers would come back terse no matter what this toggle says. Cockpit's agents now run against an isolated config and never load it, unless you switch on the Use my global CLI config capability.

18. Terminal, Files, Browser

Toolbar buttons for embedded terminal (shell), file manager, and web browser — without leaving Cockpit.

19. Accumulator

Extract knowledge from PDFs: extract → chunk → summarize → store. Local pipeline, Ollama-powered.

20. Context menus

Right-click anywhere for Cockpit-native menus. Chat: Copy, Select All, Save. Prompt: Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Save.

21. Notes (internal)

The sticky-note tab in the left sidebar — a Markdown notebook kept inside Cockpit. Create/edit notes, auto-summarize & tag with a local ≤4B model, and Chat pulls relevant notes into your prompt as context (RAG).

22. Notepad (local folder)

The Notepad button (left toolbar) opens the same notebook over a local folder you choose (e.g. an existing Markdown vault). Tick +other to include the internal notes read-only.

23. Deep search

The neurology button on Snippets & Sources runs semantic (meaning-based) search via local embeddings — finds by concept, not just keywords. Build the index once from the search dialog.

24. GLM-4 (local)

A strong 9B local model under Tier 1 in the Ollama dropdown. In Model Manager (F8): pull glm4, then Create glm4-cockpit for a GPU-tuned build. Manual/scheduled use (over the ≤4B auto limit).

25. Z.ai worker

The GLM family (GLM-4.6/4.5, free -flash) is available as a Worker — add a Z.ai key in Workers.

26. About

Click the logo (top-left) for app info, version, and license.

27. File & folder picker

Attach, Notepad, and all imports use a themed Cockpit file/folder picker — navigate the server, create folders (create_new_folder → type + Enter), pick files. No browser dialogs.

28. Library = knowledge base

Right sidebar Library holds books, articles, magazines (PDF/EPUB/DOCX/MD…). Add a file via the picker, or Scan folders to bulk-index a folder. Cockpit extracts the text so it's keyword- and semantically searchable — for you and the agents.

29. Scan folders

The create_new_folder button on Library/Snippets/Sources manages which folders Cockpit indexes. Add folders, Save & rescan.

30. Deep search

The neurology button runs semantic (meaning-based) search over your snippets, sources, library, and chats. Build the index once, then describe what you need.

31. Power Combos (Tier 0)

Multi-model recipes — several small local Ollama models run together (parallel/sequential/judge patterns) on one task, then merge into a single answer. 705 combos across 8 categories, browsable/collapsible by category in the Ollama card's Tier-0 dropdown — favorite the ones you use often. 150 unlock free on install; 555 more are premium — need a Content subscription — see the Marketplace. Full per-combo docs: cockpit_data/Cockpit_AllCombos_Reference.md / _Explained.md.

32. Delegate — task auto-routing

Set standing rules (toolbar → Delegate) that auto-send matching tasks to a chosen supplier/model/combo BEFORE the normally-selected agent continues — keyword match first, a small local model as fallback classifier, asks you if genuinely unclear. Not to be confused with the Rules (Directives) button, which injects static context into every prompt instead.

33. Multiple local users

The Users button (account card, top-right of the supplier strip) manages several local logins on one machine — each gets fully separate data (tools/skills/combos/chats/their own Cockpit Account subscription). Useful for a shared family/work computer. Sign out and Change password live in the same card.

34. Supplier Slots (CLI aliasing)

Card 1 ("Claude") and Card 2 ("Gemini") slots can be reassigned to a DIFFERENT paid CLI supplier (e.g. Codex, Qwen Code) or a free REST fallback (Groq, etc.) — the gear/tune icon on each supplier card, or the settings Slots button on the account card. The card's name, model list, and CLI-launch button all follow the assigned supplier automatically.

35. Cockpit Account & Marketplace

Click the license status text (top-left) or the account chip (top-right) to sign in/register, browse the Marketplace (community skills/tools/themes/Power Combos), and manage your subscription/credits. Local features never require an account — this is purely for the online/shared-content layer.

36. Background Tasks & Scheduler

Background Tasks — long-running autonomous goals that keep working while you do something else. Jobs (Scheduler) — cron-driven recurring tasks (e.g. nightly summaries), separate from the orchestrator's own one-off "Schedule" option in Plan mode.

37. Transcriber

Extract text from audio/video files (local whisper.cpp) beyond the quick mic-dictation button — batch processing, with analyze/compile/download/HTML export options.

38. Pending Proposals

When an agent proposes a file edit rather than applying it directly, it lands here for your review — approve or reject before anything touches disk.

39. Unit Map

The Map button (Files tab) scans a project's Pascal/PHP source and generates a structural map (units/classes/procedures) as Markdown+JSON — gives an agent fast navigational context on a codebase without reading every file.

40. Agentic workflow patterns

See the Agentic Workflow Patterns help topic for guidance on when to use Single vs Pipeline vs Broadcast vs Plan vs Combos for a given task shape.

41. Your own CLI config

Agents Cockpit starts do not read your personal ~/.claude hooks, plugins, skills or global memory — only your login, so you never sign in twice. Switch on Use my global CLI config (Settings → Capabilities) to share your own setup with them deliberately.

41. Effort levels

Claude/Gemini cards have an effort dropdown (low → max) controlling reasoning depth — higher = slower + more tokens, better for hard problems. Pick the level matching task complexity.

42. Font & typography

The Aa button (toolbar) opens font family, size, bold/italic/underline, and reset — applies across the whole UI, separate from the color Theme.

cards.title: Supplier card elements
cards.body:
Each supplier card in the top strip contains several interactive elements:

Card layout

  • Card header — supplier name + colored indicator. Click anywhere on the card to make it the active agent.
  • Status dot — green = session running, dim = stopped.
  • Model dropdown — select which model to use. Claude: opus/sonnet/haiku. Gemini: pro/flash. Ollama: any pulled model.
  • Effort dropdown (Claude/Gemini only) — reasoning depth: low → max.

Usage bar

  • Thin colored bar showing token consumption.
  • Color shifts amber → orange as quota fills.
  • Hover for exact numbers (input/output/cached tokens).
  • Right-click to reset session counters (Ollama/Workers).

Tune button (settings)

  • Opens card configuration — edit model lists, effort options, and raw JSON config.
  • Changes are saved per-supplier.

Workers card extras

  • Provider dropdown — switch between Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras, etc.
  • Discover — fetch available models from the provider's API.
  • Quota bars — per-provider daily/hourly call limits with color coding.

a2a.title: A2A — agent to agent
a2a.body:
Cockpit can be reached by another agent, or by another Cockpit, over the A2A protocol (agent card, message/send, task state, cancel). Open it from Hive → A2A.

  • It is off by default. Turning it on mints a token; a caller must send it as X-Cockpit-A2A-Token (or Authorization: Bearer …).
  • Only callers from the addresses you list are accepted — one per line: an IP, a CIDR range (192.168.1.0/24), or * for any. The default is this machine only.
  • A peer's message is dispatched to your active agent and can write into your projects, exactly like a prompt you typed. Treat the token like a password.
  • Traffic can be Dario-10S encrypted for relay use with the header X-Cockpit-Encrypted: 1.

Typical use: a second Cockpit on another machine delegates a task here, or a home-grown script asks your local agents for work without a browser.

transcriber.title: Transcriber
transcriber.body:
The Transcriber extracts and analyzes YouTube video transcripts, generating structured PDF documents.

Pipeline

  1. Extract — paste a YouTube URL. Cockpit uses yt-dlp to fetch subtitles/auto-captions and video metadata (title, channel, duration).
  2. Analyze — an Ollama model sections the transcript into structural segments with "How it Works" and "Best For" fields per section, plus key takeaways.
  3. Compile — generates a protanopia-safe SVG overview chart and a full HTML document with dark-slate background, cyan/orange accents. Optionally compiles to PDF.
  4. Download — download as PDF or HTML.

Access

Click the Trans button in the top toolbar. The panel shows input, progress, analysis results, and a list of past transcriptions.

Requirements

  • yt-dlp — must be installed for transcript extraction.
  • Ollama — any model for analysis (uses the selected Ollama model).
  • Brave browser (optional) — for PDF compilation via headless printing.

Past transcriptions

All transcriptions are saved in cockpit_data/transcriptions/. Click any past item to reload it or download its PDF.

workflows.title: Agentic Workflow Patterns
workflows.body:
Cockpit supports the 9 foundational agentic AI workflow patterns. Understanding these helps you pick the right mode for each task.

The 9 Patterns

1. Prompt ChainingSequential LLM calls — output of step N feeds step N+1. Cockpit: Pipeline mode.
2. ParallelizationFork-join: same input to multiple LLMs, aggregate results. Cockpit: Broadcast mode + Plan voter system.
3. RouterClassify input, route to optimal workflow. Cockpit: Auto-routing via style/mode selection.
4. Orchestrator-WorkerCentral planner decomposes goals, delegates to workers. Cockpit: Plan mode (orchestrator.php).
5. Evaluator-OptimizerGenerator + evaluator in feedback loop until quality met. Cockpit: Sequence verify_step gates.
6. Autonomous WorkflowAgent loops: act → observe → decide → repeat. Cockpit: Claude/Gemini CLI tool-use sessions.
7. ReflectionSelf-correction within a single generation. Cockpit: High-effort mode + style directives.
8. ReWooPlan all steps upfront, execute concurrently. Cockpit: Plan mode with schedule (decoupled planning).
9. Plan & ExecuteFull plan → task queue → sequential execution with tracking. Cockpit: Plan-and-Sequence with guardrails.

Which to use?

  • 70% of tasks need only Prompt Chaining (#1) or Routing (#3) — use Single or Pipeline mode.
  • Complex goals with subtasks → Plan mode (#4 Orchestrator-Worker, #9 Plan & Execute).
  • Quality-critical output → Sequence with verify gates (#5 Evaluator-Optimizer).
  • Multi-perspective → Broadcast mode (#2 Parallelization).
  • Overnight batch work → Schedule (#8 ReWoo pattern).

Key principle

Avoid unnecessary multi-agent overhead. Start with the simplest pattern. Only escalate to orchestrator/sequence when the task genuinely requires decomposition.

bgtasks.title: Background Tasks
bgtasks.body:
Launch and monitor autonomous goal loops and recurring jobs.

  • New goal — give an agent a standing goal; it loops observe→think→act until done or budget exhausted
  • Recurring — repeat jobs on interval (hourly, daily, weekly)
  • Kill — stop a running task immediately
  • Log — view step-by-step progress of goal loops

Access: Tasks button in toolbar or topbar. Runs via scheduler cron.

logout.title: Sign Out
logout.body:
Signs you out of Cockpit and returns to the login screen.

Access: small logout icon in the supplier strip (top-right area, near username).

Sessions are 24 hours. After signing out you need username + password to re-enter.

chgpass.title: Change Password
chgpass.body:
Change your Cockpit login password.

Access: key icon in the supplier strip (top-right, next to logout).

Requires current password + new password (min 6 chars) + confirmation.

supplier-slots.title: Supplier slots
supplier-slots.body:
The supplier slots manager (gear on the supplier strip) configures the three primary supplier roles:

  • Primary — your paid-subscription CLI agent (e.g. Claude via the Claude CLI / Pro subscription). Planner & automator. Re-login with claude → /login if it expires.
  • Fallback — a free online agent (e.g. Gemini). Cockpit calls Gemini via its REST API key (the free CLI OAuth was discontinued) — drop a free AI Studio key in cockpit_data/gemini_api_key.txt.
  • Local — Ollama, always free/offline. Its model dropdown also hosts the bolt Power Combos (see the Combos topic).

star Favorites: every selector — Ollama models, Combos, Workers, Tools — has a star/star star. Starred items float to the top of their group and persist on your machine.

Changing slots needs a Restart (the button reloads the agent loops).

Stay Free and Free agents only. Stay Free is a one-time action that picks free agents for the cards; Free agents only (Toolbar → Privacy) is the standing rule that refuses paid agents when you send. They are linked by default: Stay Free also turns the rule on, and while it is on this dialog disables the paid agents. You can untie them in Privacy & spending.

caps.title: Usage Caps
caps.body:
Set daily token and cost limits per supplier to prevent surprise bills.

  • Daily token cap — max tokens per day (0 = unlimited)
  • Daily cost cap — max USD per day (0 = unlimited)
  • Warn % — show warning when usage reaches this percentage

Caps are advisory: warns at threshold, soft-blocks at cap. Disabled by default — enable per supplier.

Access: speedometer icon next to cost tiers in the status bar.

codefolding.title: Code Folding
codefolding.body:
Long code blocks (over 15 lines) are automatically collapsed in chat output. Click the header bar of any code block to expand or collapse it.

  • Collapsed blocks show the language label, line count, and copy/save buttons
  • Click anywhere on the header to toggle
  • Short blocks (15 lines or fewer) start expanded

Consecutive system messages (4+) are also grouped and collapsed to reduce clutter.

videoattach.title: Video Attachments
videoattach.body:
Attach video files (MP4, WebM, MKV, MOV, etc.) to analyze their content.

Processing pipeline:

  1. Keyframe extraction — FFmpeg extracts up to 8 scene-change frames
  2. Vision analysis — each keyframe described by local vision model (gemma3:4b)
  3. Audio transcription — audio track extracted and transcribed via Whisper

Combined visual + audio description is injected into the prompt for the AI agent.

Requirements: ffmpeg (keyframes + audio), gemma3:4b via Ollama (vision), whisper (transcription). Falls back gracefully if any tool is missing.

about.title: About AI Cockpit
about.body: Click the logo (top-left) to open the About window — app name, version, author, license (Apache-2.0), and the stack. All processing is local unless you explicitly use a paid API provider.

filepicker.title: File / folder picker
filepicker.body:
Cockpit uses one themed file/folder picker everywhere (no browser dialogs) — for Attach, the Notepad folder, imports, tools input, and library.

How to use

  • Click into folders to navigate; ↑ Up goes to the parent.
  • Type or paste a path in the field + Go to jump anywhere.
  • create_new_folder → inline name field, Enter to create and enter it.
  • show hidden reveals dotfiles.
  • Modes: pick a folder, open a file, or save (with a filename).

Since Cockpit runs locally, picked files are read by the server directly — no upload.

scanfolders.title: Scan folders
scanfolders.body:
The create_new_folder button on Library / Snippets / Sources manages the folders Cockpit scans to auto-index files.

  • Add folder — pick a folder via the Cockpit picker.
  • Remove any folder from the list.
  • Save & rescan — saves and re-indexes. For Library, text is also extracted so files become searchable.

deepsearch.title: Deep (semantic) search
deepsearch.body:
The neurology button on Snippets, Sources, and Library runs semantic search — finds by meaning, not just keywords — using local nomic-embed-text embeddings.

How to use

  1. Open Deep Search, click Build index once (embeds snippets, sources, library content, and chats).
  2. Describe what you're looking for in plain language.
  3. Results rank by conceptual similarity; click to open.

Re-build after adding new content. Requires Ollama running with nomic-embed-text pulled.

notes.title: Notes (internal)
notes.body:
The Notes tab (left sidebar) is a Markdown note store kept inside Cockpit (cockpit_data/notes/).

Two stores, one panel

The scope dropdown switches between Internal (Cockpit's own notes) and Folder (your local Notepad folder — see the Notepad button). Tick +other to also search the other store read-only; opening a read-only note and saving copies it into the current store.

AI

  • Process now — summarize + auto-tag the note with a local ≤4B model.
  • Auto-AI (settings settings) — do that automatically on every save. Default off.
  • Chat — pulls the most relevant notes (across the selected scopes) into your prompt as context, then you ask your question (RAG).

GLM-4 and other >4B models are never auto-used here (auto policy). Notes are flat Markdown files — easy to back up.

notepad.title: Notepad (local folder)
notepad.body:
The Notepad button opens the Notes panel bound to a local folder you choose — an AI-aware Markdown notebook over an existing folder (e.g. an Obsidian/Markdown vault). On first use it asks for the folder path (the server reads/writes Markdown files there).

Same engine as internal Notes: create/edit/search, summarize + tag with a local ≤4B model, and 'Chat' to use the folder's notes as context. Tick +other to also include Cockpit's internal notes read-only.

Set or change the folder anytime in Notes settings (settings).

glm4.title: GLM-4 (local, tuned)
glm4.body:
GLM-4 9B (Zhipu) is a strong local model for CRUD, long-context, and agentic/tool work — listed under Tier 1 in the Ollama dropdown.

It's a 9B model (>4B)

Per Cockpit's safety policy, automatic/background tasks never auto-load models over 4B. GLM-4 is therefore manual / scheduled use only — pick it deliberately; it won't be chosen for auto jobs.

One-click tuned model

On a 4 GB VRAM card the full model can't fit, so it runs split GPU/CPU. In the Model Manager (F8): pull glm4, then click Create glm4-cockpit — it builds a tuned variant (num_gpu 12, num_ctx 8192, temp 0.2). Lower num_gpu if it crashes (OOM on Cinnamon), raise it for more speed.

Then select glm4-cockpit in the Ollama Tier 1 dropdown. Expect ~4–10 tok/s — ideal for rest-hour/scheduled work, not real-time chat.

usermgr.title: User Manager
usermgr.body:
Admin only. Create, edit, and delete Cockpit user accounts.

  • Add user — set username, password, and role (Admin, Normal, or Viewer)
  • Edit — change username, password, or role for any user
  • Delete — remove a user (cannot delete yourself)

Roles: Admin = full access + user management. Normal = standard access. Viewer = read-only.

Access: group icon in the supplier strip top-right controls.

combos.title: Power Combos
combos.body:
Power Combos run several local models (Ollama, LocalAI, or a mix of both) together as one recipe — in parallel, in sequence, or with a judge — and show each model's output side by side. Both the Ollama and LocalAI model dropdowns have their own Combos section, same layout either side (master row with total count + filter + collapse/expand-all, categorized combos, a Needs both backends section for mixed-runner combos, then the model list).

705 combos across 8 categories, tagged by category and available at Tier-0. Groups are collapsible now (click a category header, or ⊟/⊞ all in the Tier-0 header) — with this many, browsing collapsed-by-default is usually easier.

How to use (the non-obvious bits)

  • Where: open the Ollama or LocalAI card's model dropdown — each has its own Combos section near the top. Combos run when that card is the active agent; mixed-backend combos (steps split across both) show up under Needs both backends in both dropdowns regardless of which catalog they were actually saved in.
  • Run: pick a combo (label shows bolt), type your prompt, press Execute. It replaces the single-model run with the multi-model recipe. Pick a normal model again to leave combo mode.
  • Find fast: type in the filter box in the Tier-0 header; browse by category; click star to favorite — favorites float to a star group on top.
  • Patterns: parallel = a grid (models work at once, output divides by role); sequential = a pipeline (each step feeds the next, ↓); judge = a verdict on top + the candidates collapsible below.
  • Models are tiny (0.5–3B) so output is fast but modest — the value is the division of labour by role, not deep reasoning. Sequential combos are slower (models run back-to-back).
  • RAG combos (marked) pull from your knowledge center; they widen context (num_ctx) automatically.
  • VRAM: each combo shows ~MB. Keep parallel combos under ~3.5 GB (4 GB card). Needs Ollama OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL/MAX_LOADED_MODELS ≥ the step count for true concurrency.
  • Greyed-out = a required model isn't pulled — hover the row to see exactly which model is missing, tagged with which backend it's missing from (Ollama or LocalAI). Pull it there to enable.
  • Combo results are saved to the chat and survive reload (as text).

Free vs. protected

The 50 original combos ship free and plaintext — they always work, on any machine, no account needed. The other 185 (and any future curated packs) are encrypted at rest, bound to this machine + your account license — a copied file is inert on someone else's install. This only stops casual copying, not determined reverse-engineering by observing behavior; that's an accepted, honest limit, same as any local-execution product.

If a protected pack exists on disk but won't decrypt (wrong machine, expired/missing license), Tier-0 shows an amber warning instead of silently showing fewer combos — sign in with the account that downloaded them, or re-download from the Marketplace.

Your own combos

Click ＋ new in either dropdown's master row to build your own combo — id, name, pattern, category (pick one or type a brand-new one — it creates the group on the fly), description, and steps. Each step has its own model dropdown (built from your actually-installed Ollama + LocalAI models, not free-text) and its own backend picker (Default / Ollama / LocalAI) — mix backends across steps and it becomes a dual combo. Add a judge model+instructions for judge-pattern, same dropdown picker. Saved instantly, always plain JSON, never encrypted (it’s already yours). Edit (edit) or delete (delete) any combo tagged · mine — Edit stays clickable even when the combo is currently missing a model, since that's exactly when you'd use it.

Publish to the Marketplace: Account panel → Marketplace → ⊕ Publish → kind My Combo (earns credit) → pick one of yours. Needs a Content-tier subscription (same as publishing a Skill or Tool). Earns the same give-back credit as any other content — downloads and usage both count, same pools, same payout mechanics.

Downloading someone else’s combo merges it into your own Tier-0 (tagged · by <name>) — before it downloads, Cockpit checks each of its models against your actually-installed Ollama and LocalAI models (each checked against the specific backend it runs on) and shows you which you're missing, so you can back out instead of downloading something you can’t run yet.

Published one by mistake? The languageclose icon on your own published combos unpublishes it from the Marketplace (your local copy stays).

The 705 combos, by category

computer Coding198
description Office & Docs141
public Language114
palette Image69
psychology Learning69
bar_chart Data57
edit Creative42
accessible Accessibility15

Full per-combo descriptions (all 705, what each one does and why) live in cockpit_data/Cockpit_AllCombos_Reference.md (quick lookup table) and cockpit_data/Cockpit_AllCombos_Explained.md (detailed rationale per combo) — too long to usefully inline here; open them from a file manager or editor. The 150 free combos are tagged "initial": true in combos.json if you want to filter to just those.

codeblocks.title: Code tab (right sidebar)
codeblocks.body:
The Code tab collects code blocks extracted from agent responses (via %%CREATE%%-style markers), separate from the chat's own inline code folding.

  • Upload — add a code file from disk directly.
  • Auto toggle — when on (default), new code blocks in agent responses are captured here automatically as they arrive.
  • Refresh — reload the list from disk.

This is a per-project store — files land under the project's code/ folder.

knowledge.title: Knowledge Library (right sidebar)
knowledge.body:
The Library tab holds long-form reference material — books, articles, docs — indexed for search and RAG context.

  • Search — keyword search across indexed content.
  • ＋ (add) — pick a file, or add a folder to scan.
  • Add location — register a path or URL manually (typed, not picked).
  • Rescan — re-index configured folders, extract text.
  • Scan folders — manage which folders get auto-scanned.
  • Deep search — meaning-based (semantic) search via local embeddings, not just keyword match.
  • Refresh — reload the index.

Locations are read-only references — content is indexed, not duplicated into Cockpit's storage.

snippets.title: Snippets (right sidebar)
snippets.body:
The Snippets tab stores short, reusable code/text blocks — one file per snippet, indexed for search.

  • Search — keyword search across snippets.
  • ＋ (add) — create one manually.
  • Upload — add a snippet file from disk.
  • Rescan — rebuild the index from the storage directory.
  • Scan folders — manage auto-scanned folders for Snippets.
  • Deep search — semantic search via local embeddings.
  • Refresh — reload the index from disk.

Agents can propose new snippets from chat (right-click → Save to Snippets, or F2) — proposals need approval before they're saved.

sources.title: Sources (right sidebar)
sources.body:
The Sources tab tracks whole external projects/programs you reference — not individual files like Snippets, but entire codebases or programs.

  • Search — keyword search across registered sources.
  • ＋ (add) — register a source project manually.
  • Upload — add a source file or .zip from disk.
  • Rescan — rebuild the index from the storage directory.
  • Scan folders — manage auto-scanned folders for Sources.
  • Deep search — semantic search via local embeddings.
  • Refresh — reload the index from disk.

Agents can propose new sources from chat — proposals need approval before they're saved.

delegate.title: Delegate — task auto-routing
delegate.body:
Set standing rules that auto-delegate matching tasks to a chosen supplier/model/combo — automatically, regardless of which module (Single/Pipeline/Broadcast/Plan/Combos) is currently handling your prompt.

How matching works

  1. Keyword/phrase — set when creating a rule. Fast, free, exact.
  2. Small local model — if no keyword hits (or it's ambiguous), a tiny Ollama model tries to classify the task.
  3. Ask you — if the model isn't confident either, you'll be shown the candidate rules to pick from (or none).

When a rule fires

The target (worker/combo/Ollama model) runs first, its result is folded into your prompt as context, then the normally-selected agent continues with that included — the rule augments the task, it doesn't replace it.

Not to be confused with the Rules (Directives) button — that injects static context into every prompt for every supplier. This routes specific tasks to a different supplier.

account.title: Cockpit Account (SaaS)
account.body:
Your online AI Cockpit account — separate from the local app login you use to open Cockpit on this machine. Click the license status text (top-left), or the button showing your name in the account card (it carries a small cog in the Full edition), to open it. In the Stand-alone edition that button opens the local user manager instead.

  • Sign in / Register — free account, no card required for local features.
  • Tier chip — shows Free / Content / Everywhere / Combined.
  • Marketplace — browse/publish community skills, tools, themes, and Power Combos.
  • Account portal — profile, registered machines, credits balance, subscription/renewal choice.
  • Change user — switch between several registered accounts on this machine without re-entering credentials each time (a roster, not re-login).

Since 2026-07-02, each local app user (see the Users/usermgr topic) gets their own separate Cockpit Account — a shared machine can have several people, each with their own subscription.

marketplace.title: Marketplace & Combo Store
marketplace.body:
Community content — browse, download, and (if you're the account owner) publish skills/tools/themes/prompts/worker cards/pipelines, plus Power Combos (see the Combos topic).

  • Kind filter — narrow the list to one content type, including "Power Combos".
  • Free vs earnable — free items (themes/prompts) are open to everyone; earnable items (skills/tools/etc) need a Content-tier subscription. Combos have their own base(free)/premium(Content-tier) split.
  • ＋ Publish — upload something you made. Combo publishing is admin-only (curated, not open upload).
  • Download — installs straight into the matching local panel (Skills/Tools/Capabilities) or, for combos, into the encrypted local combo store — no manual file placement needed.

Everything downloaded runs 100% locally after that — the marketplace is just discovery/distribution, not a hosted execution service.
